I farm the way I know best: I keep cotton as my main crop because I have grown it for many years, I know how to watch it closely, and it still gives me cash income. My family has some people working off-farm, so I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too labor-heavy. I will put the biggest share of my 18 mu into cotton, then keep some wheat and maize so I have grain and I spread my risk. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on a steady but not excessive number of irrigations, and I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps me get a steadier stand and yield. I will fertilize each crop at a moderate level, not too low and not too aggressive, because I want stable output and manageable cost. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and fits how I usually prepare land.
